## Replication with new data {#replication-with-new-data .smaller}

::: {.small}
- A replication asks **the same question of new data**: here, later waves of the Standard Eurobarometer, which kept asking what the EU means to people
- SCORE ran one: fourteen Standard waves fielded between 2013 and 2019, in the member states and the United Kingdom
- Its verdict: a **positive** coefficient for unemployment, not significant, so the replication was **not successful** by the criterion of SCORE
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
A failed replication says that the claim did not hold in those data with that analysis. On its own it cannot say whether the data, the analysis or the world had changed.
:::

::: notes
The last of the three Rs is replication: the same question, new data. For this claim the new data exist, because the Standard Eurobarometer kept asking people what the EU means to them after the original study ended in 2013. SCORE commissioned exactly this: a team took fourteen Standard waves fielded between 2013 and 2019, in the member states and the United Kingdom, and fitted a model like that of the original author. Its verdict was a positive coefficient for unemployment, the opposite sign to the claim, and not significant, so the replication was not successful by the criterion that SCORE had set. [advance] Hold that verdict carefully. It tells you that the claim did not hold in those data with that analysis. It cannot tell you on its own which of the three moved: the data, the analysis, or a relationship that changed over a decade.
:::

## The question after 2013 {#the-question-after-2013 .smaller}

::: {.small}
- The question was asked in Standard waves until spring 2024, with a gap in the winter of 2020–21, and not in the three Standard waves from autumn 2024 to autumn 2025
- From EB 92.3, at the end of 2019, the answer list has a **fifteenth category**: "Quality of life of future generations"
- The member states changed: 27 in the paper, 28 with Croatia in the SCORE replication, 27 again once the United Kingdom left in 2020
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
A share of mentions divides by the number of items mentioned, so a new category changes the outcome even for a respondent whose answers on the old items are the same.
:::

::: notes
If you wanted to replicate this claim yourself, what would you find? The question kept appearing in the Standard waves until the spring of 2024, apart from one gap in the winter of 2020 to 2021, and it is absent from the three Standard waves after that. From the autumn wave of 2019 the answer list carries a fifteenth category, the quality of life of future generations. The member states changed as well: twenty-seven in the paper, twenty-eight in the SCORE replication, which added Croatia and kept the United Kingdom, and twenty-seven again once the United Kingdom left. [advance] Each of these is a measurement decision. The outcome of the paper is a share of mentions, so a new answer category changes the denominator, and a respondent who gives the same answers on the old items gets a different score.
:::

## Decisions to fix in advance {#decisions-to-fix-in-advance .smaller}

::: {.small}
| Decision | For a replication of your analysis |
|:--|:--|
| **The claim and its test** | which coefficient, which sign, which threshold counts as success |
| **The data** | which waves, which countries, which unemployment series |
| **The measurement** | the new fifteenth category, the respondents who mention nothing |
| **The analysis** | the model of your analyst, as you reproduced it, unchanged |
| **The report** | what you will say if the result differs, and what if it agrees |
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
All five can be fixed **before the new data are opened**, which is what a preregistration is for.
:::

::: notes
So a replication of the analysis you reproduced this morning involves decisions of five kinds, and every one of them can be taken before you look at the new data. Which coefficient you will read, which sign the claim predicts and which threshold counts as success. Which waves, which countries and which unemployment series, given that the series you reproduced may have been revised since. What you do with the new answer category and with the respondents who mention nothing. Which model, and the natural answer is the one you reproduced, unchanged, because that is what makes it a replication rather than a new analysis. And what you will say whichever way it comes out. [advance] Fixing those in advance is exactly what a preregistration does, and it is the last task of the day.
:::
